mainTopic: The six inspected lambs, how new Temple vessels are first put into use (חינוך), and donated incense
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question on the משנה about keeping six inspected lambs 'enough for שבת and the two days of ראש השנה.' The count seems to reach seven, so the גמרא says six is a general number and the phrase is only a memory aid, which the word 'כדי' supports. Next comes the משנה about a missed morning תמיד. The גמרא fills in missing words: a new מזבח must begin with the morning lamb, but once it is in use the afternoon lamb is brought anyway, which a ברייתא learns from the פסוק that calls the afternoon lamb 'the second.' רבי שמעון limits this to cases of force or mistake, and רבא explains that only the guilty כהנים lose the right to bring it, while missed incense is always burned because כהנים treasure that service. The גמרא then shows that תנאים disagree whether a new golden altar starts with the morning or afternoon incense, and אביי supports the afternoon view from the פסוק about fixing the lamps. It also explains that a new שלחן starts, and its bread becomes holy, only on שבת, just as the מנורה starts with its evening lighting. Finally, a ברייתא about the one-time incense of the נשיאים on the outer altar leads to a challenge about whether an individual or the community may ever donate incense, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The count still comes out to seven lambs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that, whichever way you count it, the number of lambs needed is seven and not six.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, it comes out to seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on the משנה that says six inspected lambs are enough. By the count worked out before this, seven lambs would be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier calculations tried to explain the משנה's number of six. The גמרא now says that whatever approach you take, you still need seven, so the number six in the משנה does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case / either way
It comes out to seven

phrases.english: In any case, they are seven!
phrases.notes: The lambs kept ready for the daily תמיד: the משנה said six, but the count comes to seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of how many inspected lambs the משנה requires.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that six inspected lambs are kept on hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every way of counting the lambs needed for שבת and the two days of ראש השנה reaches seven, so the number six does not work.

steps.title: The משנה is speaking generally, and the phrase is just a memory aid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה gives a general rule for the whole year. The mention of שבת and ראש השנה is only a reminder of the number, not an exact calculation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תנא is speaking in general. And what does he mean by 'enough for שבת and the two days of יום טוב of ראש השנה'? It is just a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem by changing how we read the משנה. Six is the general number of lambs always kept ready, and the words about שבת and ראש השנה are only a sign to help us remember it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we read 'enough for שבת and the two days of ראש השנה' as an exact count for that case, and that count gave seven. Now the phrase is read as a סימן: three days with two lambs each equals six. It is a reminder of the number, not a real accounting of those days.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the משנה
Is speaking in general terms
A sign or memory aid

phrases.english: Rather, the tanna is standing in general terms,
phrases.notes: He means the six lambs are the general number kept on hand all year, not a count for one special week.

phrases.english: and what is 'enough for Shabbat'

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה?
phrases.english: and the two festival days of Rosh HaShana?
Merely a mnemonic.
phrases.notes: Three days with two lambs a day gives six, so the phrase just helps you remember the number.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by reading the משנה differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'enough for שבת and the two days of ראש השנה' is an exact count of the lambs needed, which comes to seven.
steps.terutzMaskana: Six is a general standing number, and the phrase is only a סימן for remembering it.
steps.whatToRemember: Six is the general number of inspected lambs. 'שבת and the two days of ראש השנה' is only a סימן (3 days × 2 lambs = 6).

steps.title: The משנה's exact wording supports the memory-aid reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the משנה's wording fits the answer: it says 'enough for שבת,' not 'for שבת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise this way. The משנה says 'enough for שבת' and does not say 'for שבת and for the two days of יום טוב of ראש השנה.' Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from a small detail in the משנה's language.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Enough for' (כדי) suggests an amount the size of what those days need, a reminder of the size. 'For שבת' would have meant lambs actually set aside for those days. Since the משנה chose 'כדי,' it fits the סימן reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise this way (a support from exact language)
Enough for / an amount equal to
Learn from it (the point is proven)

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it teaches 'sufficient for Shabbat,'
and it does not teach 'for Shabbat'

phrases.aramaic: וְלִשְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה״,
phrases.english: and for the two festival days of Rosh HaShana,'
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 2 from the משנה's precise wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the phrase about שבת and ראש השנה is only a סימן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's use of the word 'כדי' (enough for) rather than 'ל' (for)
steps.whatToRemember: The single word 'כדי' shows that the משנה is giving a measure, not lambs set aside for specific days.

steps.title: The משנה about a missed morning offering, and רבי שמעון's comment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה about a lamb that was not brought in the morning. רבי שמעון adds that the whole incense was offered in the afternoon, because the golden altar is first put into use only with incense.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If they did not bring a lamb in the morning,' and so on. רבי שמעון said: And all of it was offered in the afternoon, because the golden altar is put into use only with the incense of spices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה about a missed morning תמיד, along with רבי שמעון's added comment. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that missing the morning service does not cancel the afternoon one. רבי שמעון adds a new idea, חינוך, the first use of a new golden altar. He says it begins with incense, so the full amount is burned in the afternoon.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamb (here, of the תמיד)
In the afternoon
Put a vessel into use for the first time (חינוך)
The golden (incense) altar
The incense of spices

phrases.english: If they did not sacrifice a lamb in the morning, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' covers the rest of the משנה: still bring the afternoon lamb, and burn the afternoon incense even if the morning incense was missed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
And all of it was offered in the afternoon,
phrases.notes: 'All of it' means the full daily measure of incense, not just the usual afternoon half.

phrases.english: for they do not initiate the golden altar
except with the incense of spices.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A missed morning offering does not cancel the afternoon one. According to רבי שמעון, the golden altar is first put into use with incense, and the full measure is burned in the afternoon.

steps.title: Who mentioned putting the altar into use?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון talks about חינוך when the משנה never brought it up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who mentioned חינוך at all?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's comment. The first part of the משנה said nothing about a new altar, so his reasoning seems to come from nowhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון explains himself using חינוך, as if the משנה had been discussing a new altar. But the משנה, as written, speaks only of a missed morning offering, so his explanation does not seem to connect to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The first use of a new altar or vessel
Who mentioned it? (it was never brought up)

phrases.english: Initiation — who mentioned its name?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's comment quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first part of the משנה never discussed a new altar, so a comment based on חינוך does not fit.

steps.title: The משנה has missing words about the altar's first use
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing words. If the altar has not yet been put into use, they do not bring the afternoon lamb without the morning one. If it already has been, they do bring it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches: If they did not bring a lamb in the morning, they should not bring one in the afternoon. When is this said? When the מזבח has not yet been put into use. But if the מזבח has already been put into use, they should bring it in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in missing words in the משנה. With those words added, the משנה is about חינוך, so רבי שמעון's comment fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The completed משנה splits the case in two. For a new מזבח that has not been put into use, skipping the morning lamb means no afternoon lamb, because the altar must be started with the morning תמיד. Once the altar is already in use, the afternoon lamb is brought anyway. This is how חינוך enters the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words
When is this said? (limits a rule to a specific case)
Has already been put into use

steps.confusionAlert: The completed משנה actually says NOT to bring the afternoon lamb when the morning one was missed. That applies only to a brand-new מזבח. An altar already in use still gets the afternoon lamb.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a new מזבח must begin with the morning תמיד. After that first use, a missed morning offering no longer cancels the afternoon one.

phrases.english: It is incomplete, and this is what it teaches:
If they did not sacrifice a lamb in the morning —
they should not sacrifice in the afternoon.
In what case are these words said?
When the altar was not yet initiated,
but if the altar was initiated —
they should sacrifice in the afternoon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by filling in missing words in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מחסרא: missing words are filled into the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה simply says to bring the afternoon offering even if the morning one was missed, with no mention of חינוך.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה separates a new מזבח that is not yet in use (no afternoon lamb) from one already in use (bring the afternoon lamb), so חינוך is part of the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: A new מזבח must be started with the morning תמיד. Once it is in use, the afternoon תמיד is brought even if the morning one was missed.

steps.title: רבי שמעון limits the rule to forced or mistaken cases
steps.stepSummary: Finishing the corrected משנה, רבי שמעון says the rule applies when the כהנים were אנוסין or שוגגין. If they skipped the morning lamb on purpose, they do not bring the afternoon lamb. Missed incense is still burned in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: When does this apply? When they were forced or made a mistake. But if they did it on purpose and did not offer the lamb in the morning, they should not offer it in the afternoon. If they did not burn incense in the morning, they should burn it in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last part of the משנה as the גמרא just filled it in. רבי שמעון explains when the rule 'if the altar was already in use, we still bring the afternoon lamb' applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step taught that once the altar is in use, a missed morning lamb does not stop the afternoon lamb. רבי שמעון narrows this. It is true only when the morning lamb was missed by force or by mistake. If it was skipped on purpose, the afternoon lamb is not brought, but incense is treated differently and is burned in the afternoon anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Forced; stopped by something outside their control
Acting by mistake, without meaning to
Acting on purpose
The incense burned on the golden altar
Afternoon (literally 'between the evenings')

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not treat the lamb and the incense the same way. Skipping the lamb on purpose cancels the afternoon lamb, but missed incense is still burned in the afternoon.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: When [does this apply]?
At a time when they were forced or acted by mistake,
but if they acted on purpose
and did not offer a lamb in the morning,
they should not offer one in the afternoon.
If they did not burn incense in the morning,
they should burn it in the afternoon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the corrected משנה from step 6 with רבי שמעון's limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the altar is in use, the afternoon lamb is brought only if the morning lamb was missed by force or by mistake. If it was skipped on purpose, the afternoon lamb is not brought. Missed incense is still burned in the afternoon.

steps.title: What is the source for the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a missed morning lamb stops the afternoon lamb before the altar's חינוך.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the afternoon lamb is not brought without the morning lamb, but only before the altar is in use. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (a request for the source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters [learned]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the משנה's rule is clear, the גמרא looks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that the afternoon lamb is not brought without the morning lamb before the altar's חינוך.

steps.title: The verse calls the afternoon lamb 'the second'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'and the second lamb you shall offer in the afternoon' that the afternoon lamb must be the second one, never the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'And the second lamb you shall offer in the afternoon.' The second lamb is offered in the afternoon, but the first is not offered in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא that reads a careful lesson out of the word 'second' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the afternoon lamb 'the second.' So an afternoon lamb can only be brought after a morning lamb has been brought. It can never be the first lamb offered.

keyTerms.meaning: The second lamb, which is the afternoon תמיד
First

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught: 'And the second lamb'
'you shall offer in the afternoon.'
The second [lamb is offered] in the afternoon,
but not the first in the afternoon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'second' in the פסוק teaches that an afternoon lamb cannot be the first one brought.

steps.title: The verse's limit applies only before the altar's חינוך
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the 'second, not first' rule applies only to an altar that has not yet been put into use. Once it is in use, even the first lamb of the day may be brought in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When the altar has not yet been put into use. But if the altar has been put into use, even the first one may be offered in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us when the lesson from 'second' applies. It applies only to a new altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'First' and 'second' here mean the very first and second lambs ever offered on that altar, not the first and second of each day. So the afternoon lamb is blocked only before the altar's חינוך. This matches the corrected משנה from step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (a phrase that limits a rule)
Was put into use for the first time
Altar

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the corrected משנה (step 6) comes straight from a ברייתא and a פסוק, not just from guessing.

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
When the altar has not been put into use,
but if the altar has been put into use,
even the first [may be offered] in the afternoon.
phrases.notes: Here 'the first' means the first lamb brought that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues and limits its own lesson from the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The afternoon lamb is blocked only before the altar's חינוך. Afterward, it may be brought even if it is the first lamb of the day.

steps.title: The ברייתא also brings רבי שמעון's limit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with the same words of רבי שמעון that are in the משנה. The afternoon lamb is brought only if the morning lamb was missed by force or mistake, while missed incense is burned in the afternoon anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: When does this apply? When they were forced or made a mistake. But if they did it on purpose and did not offer the lamb in the morning, they should not offer it in the afternoon. If they did not burn incense in the morning, they should burn it in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats רבי שמעון's words exactly as they appear in the משנה. This time they belong to the source the גמרא just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי שמעון's limit is attached to the ברייתא's rule about an altar that is already in use. The משנה and the ברייתא now match in every part: the new-altar rule, the in-use rule, and רבי שמעון's exception for acting on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: When? (asks when a rule applies)
They burned (the incense)
They should offer

steps.whatToRemember: Before the altar's חינוך, the afternoon lamb needs a morning lamb first, because the פסוק calls it 'second.' After the חינוך, it is brought anyway, unless the morning lamb was skipped on purpose (רבי שמעון). Missed incense is always burned in the afternoon.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: When [does this apply]?
At a time when they were forced or acted by mistake,
but if they acted on purpose
and did not offer a lamb in the morning,
they should not offer one in the afternoon.
If they did not burn incense in the morning,
they should burn it in the afternoon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא with רבי שמעון's limit on its in-use rule, using the same words as step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the altar is in use, the afternoon lamb is brought only if the morning lamb was missed by force or mistake. Missed incense is burned in the afternoon regardless.

steps.title: Should the altar sit idle because the כהנים sinned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's rule. If the כהנים skipped the morning lamb on purpose, does that mean the whole altar stops working?
steps.simpleTranslation: Just because the כהנים sinned, should the altar be idle?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי שמעון's rule that if the morning lamb was skipped on purpose, the afternoon lamb is not brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, רבי שמעון's rule means no afternoon תמיד at all that day. The גמרא finds this unreasonable. The sin belongs to the כהנים, so why should the whole altar and the people lose the afternoon offering?

keyTerms.meaning: They sinned (here: skipped the morning lamb on purpose)
The altar
Idle, unused, not working

phrases.english: But if the priests sinned,
should the altar be idle?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's rule about a deliberate skip, which was quoted in steps 7 and 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's rule that a deliberate skip of the morning lamb cancels the afternoon lamb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes no sense to punish the altar and the whole public for a sin committed by particular כהנים.

steps.title: Only the guilty כהנים may not offer the afternoon lamb
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי שמעון only meant that the guilty כהנים may not bring the afternoon lamb. Other כהנים may bring it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what he means: they themselves should not offer it, but other כהנים should offer it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by narrowing רבי שמעון's rule. It is a penalty on the guilty כהנים, not on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'they do not bring' are now read as personal: the same כהנים who skipped on purpose lose the right to bring the afternoon lamb. Other כהנים step in, so the altar is not left idle.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means, a way of explaining someone's words more exactly
Others (here: other כהנים)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי שמעון's rule is a penalty on the negligent כהנים, not a rule that the afternoon תמיד is cancelled.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what he is saying:
they should not offer it,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the same כהנים who skipped the morning lamb on purpose.

phrases.english: but others should offer it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the ruling: a penalty on specific people, not a cancellation of the service
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון meant that no afternoon lamb is brought at all, leaving the altar idle.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the guilty כהנים are barred from bringing it. Other כהנים bring the afternoon lamb.

steps.title: Why missed incense is still burned, even by the same כהנים
steps.stepSummary: If the morning incense was not burned, even on purpose, it is still burned in the afternoon. The כהנים love this service, so there is no need to penalize them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they did not burn the incense in the morning, they burn it in the afternoon. Since it does not come often, and it makes a person rich, it is dear to them, and they are not careless with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the incense is different from the lamb. Even the same כהנים may burn the missed incense in the afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The penalty for skipping the lamb was meant to stop כהנים from being careless. With incense there is no such worry. A כהן rarely gets to burn it, and it brings blessing of wealth, so כהנים treasure it and will not neglect it. That is why no penalty is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Incense burned on the golden altar
It is not common, it does not happen often
It makes a person wealthy
They are careless or negligent

phrases.english: If they did not burn incense in the morning,
they should burn it in the afternoon,
phrases.notes: Here this applies even to the same כהנים who skipped it on purpose.

phrases.english: because since it is not common, and it makes one wealthy,
it is dear to them and they are not careless.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הִקְטִירוּ קְטֹרֶת בַּבֹּקֶר, יַקְטִירוּ בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 13 explained the penalty for the lamb, this step explains why no such penalty applies to the incense.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Missed morning incense is burned in the afternoon, even by the same כהנים, because they treasure this service and there is no fear they will neglect it.
steps.whatToRemember: Lamb skipped on purpose: the guilty כהנים may not bring the afternoon lamb, but others do. Incense skipped: it is burned in the afternoon anyway, because כהנים love that service.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: a new golden altar starts with the afternoon incense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. רבי שמעון says a new golden altar is first put into use only with the afternoon incense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: And all of it was offered in the afternoon, because the golden altar is put into use only with the spice incense of the afternoon, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's words from the משנה to set up a question about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that when the golden altar is new, its first use is the afternoon incense, and then the full amount was burned. This is a new topic: which time of day starts a new golden altar. The next step will challenge it.

keyTerms.meaning: Put into use for the first time, start the service of
The golden altar, the inner altar where incense is burned
The incense of spices
Afternoon, toward evening

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: And all of it was
offered in the afternoon,
phrases.notes: 'All of it' means the full amount of incense, not just the usual half.

phrases.english: because they do not start the use of the golden altar

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּקְטֹרֶת הַסַּמִּים שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: except with the spice incense of the afternoon, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: וְכוּלָּהּ הָיְתָה קְרֵיבָה בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה about starting the use of a new golden altar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new golden altar is first put into use with the afternoon incense, and then the full amount is burned.

steps.title: A ברייתא says it starts with the morning incense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says a new golden altar is first used with the morning incense, which contradicts רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught in a ברייתא: with the spice incense of the morning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's statement with a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said the afternoon incense starts the new golden altar. The ברייתא says the morning incense does. Both cannot be right as written.

keyTerms.meaning: Dawn, morning

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
with the spice incense of the morning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement of רבי שמעון quoted in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's statement that the golden altar starts with the afternoon incense
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא directly states that the golden altar starts with the morning incense.

steps.title: It is a disagreement between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two sources simply reflect two different opinions among the תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying there is nothing to fix. Two תנאים disagree on this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not try to make both sources say the same thing. It accepts that רבי שמעון holds 'afternoon' and the ברייתא follows a different תנא who holds 'morning'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disagreement between תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not decide who is right. It only explains why the two sources say different things. אביי's next step gives a reason to prefer one side.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between authorities: the two sources reflect different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and רבי שמעון must agree, so one of them seems wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are two opinions: one תנא says morning, רבי שמעון says afternoon.

steps.title: אביי: the afternoon view makes more sense, from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the view that the golden altar starts with the afternoon incense is more reasonable, and he brings a פסוק about fixing the lamps in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It makes sense to follow the one who says it starts with the afternoon spice incense, as it is written: 'Every morning, when he fixes the lamps, he shall burn it.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes a side in the dispute and supports the afternoon view with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the morning incense to fixing the lamps of the מנורה. Fixing lamps in the morning assumes they were already lit the evening before. So it seems the service started in the evening, and the first incense would also be the afternoon incense.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it stands to reason
When he fixes or cleans (the lamps)
The lamps of the מנורה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two opinions about how a new golden altar is first used: morning incense or afternoon incense. רבי שמעון says afternoon, and אביי agrees, based on the פסוק about fixing the lamps in the morning.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It stands to reason like the one who says
with the spice incense of the afternoon,
as it is written: "Every morning
when he fixes the lamps he shall burn it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17 presents the dispute, אביי gives a reason to prefer the afternoon view.
steps.raayaObject: The view that a new golden altar is first used with the afternoon incense
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 30:7: 'Every morning when he fixes the lamps he shall burn it', which implies the lamps were already lit the evening before

steps.title: Morning cleaning proves evening lighting came first
steps.stepSummary: אביי completes his proof: cleaning the lamps in the morning assumes they were already lit the evening before.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the lamps had not been lit the evening before, what would there be to clean in the morning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's proof from the previous step. Lamps can only be cleaned in the morning if they were lit the night before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links burning the incense to working on the lamps, both in the morning and in the evening. Cleaning presupposes an earlier lighting, so the very first lamp service must be in the evening. The incense is tied to the lamps, so the first incense on a new golden altar must also be in the evening.

keyTerms.meaning: Lighting the lamps of the מנורה
Cleaning and preparing the lamps, removing old ashes and wicks
From the evening before
In the morning

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי שמעון in the משנה says a new golden altar starts with the afternoon incense.

phrases.english: If he had not done the lighting the evening before,
from where would there be cleaning in the morning?
phrases.notes: He means: there would be nothing to clean. So the lamps, and the incense tied to them, must start in the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's proof begun in step 18
steps.raayaObject: The view that a new golden altar starts with the afternoon incense
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק that ties the incense to cleaning the lamps in the morning, which only makes sense if they were lit the previous evening

steps.title: What is the source for starting with the morning incense?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the other opinion relies on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says a new golden altar starts with the morning incense, what is his source?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other view, from the ברייתא, and asks where it comes from. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי just showed that the afternoon view makes sense. Now the גמרא wants to know what reasoning supports the morning view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
The incense made of spices, burned on the golden altar
Of the morning

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר בִּקְטֹרֶת הַסַּמִּים שֶׁל שַׁחַר,
phrases.english: And according to the one who says it starts with the spice incense of the morning,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the afternoon view to ask about the opposing morning view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the view that a new golden altar starts with the morning incense

steps.title: Learned from the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: The morning view learns from the outer altar, which starts with the morning תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the altar of burnt offerings. Just as there it starts with the morning תמיד, so here it starts with the morning incense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this opinion compares the golden altar to the outer altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new outer altar is first used with the morning תמיד. This opinion says the golden altar works the same way, so it starts with the morning incense. The afternoon view instead ties the incense to the lamps.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it, derives it from another case
The outer altar, where burnt offerings were brought
The daily morning offering
Just as there, so too here: a comparison between two cases

steps.whatToRemember: Afternoon view: the incense follows the lamps, which start in the evening. Morning view: the golden altar follows the outer altar, which starts in the morning.

phrases.english: He learns it from the altar of burnt offerings:
just as there it starts with the morning daily offering,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן בִּקְטֹרֶת הַסַּמִּים שֶׁל שַׁחַר.
phrases.english: so too here it starts with the morning spice incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A comparison to the outer altar, whose first use is with the morning תמיד

steps.title: The משנה on starting a new table
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a new שלחן is first used only with the לחם הפנים on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a new table was put into use only with the showbread on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about the שלחן. It is setting up a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לחם הפנים was set on the שלחן only on שבת. The משנה says a new שלחן begins its service with that שבת placement.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden table in the Temple
The showbread, twelve loaves placed on the שלחן each שבת
Putting a new vessel into use for the first time

phrases.english: And not the table,
except with the showbread on שבת.
phrases.notes: "Not the table except" means a new table is not put into use except in this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָן אֶלָּא בְּלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new שלחן is put into use only with the placing of the לחם הפנים on שבת

steps.title: Does weekday showbread become holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה implies that showbread placed on a weekday still becomes holy, only the table is not put into use.
steps.simpleTranslation: But on a weekday, is it only that the table is not put into use, while the bread still becomes holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. It seems to suggest that on a weekday only the first use fails, but the bread still becomes holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks only about the table being put into use. That could imply the bread does become holy on a weekday. But the rule is that לחם הפנים becomes holy only on שבת, so this reading seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A weekday, not שבת
Making holy: here, the showbread becoming holy on the table
But, does it then mean: introduces an implied conclusion

phrases.english: But on a weekday,
is it only that it is not put into use,
but it does become holy?!
phrases.notes: "It" here is the showbread placed on the table on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּחוֹל אִיחַנּוֹכֵי הוּא דְּלָא מִחַנַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges an implication of the משנה quoted in step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה about the שלחן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mentions only the first use, which suggests weekday bread still becomes holy. That goes against the rule that it becomes holy only on שבת.

steps.title: Both first use and holiness happen only on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is teaching that both the first use of the table and the holiness of the bread happen only on שבת, just like the מנורה starts only in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is exactly what it teaches us: the first use and the making holy of the table happen on שבת. This matches the next clause: a new מנורה is put into use only with lighting its seven lamps in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is not hinting that weekday bread becomes holy. It is teaching that everything about the table, first use and holiness, depends on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the regular, proper time of each vessel's service to show how it is put into use. On a weekday nothing happens with the bread at all. The next clause about the מנורה works the same way: it starts at its regular time, the evening lighting.

keyTerms.meaning: That itself is what it teaches us
The later clause of the משנה
The Temple candelabrum
In the afternoon, toward evening

steps.whatToRemember: Each vessel is put into use at its regular service time: the שלחן on שבת (and only then does the bread become holy), and the מנורה at the evening lighting.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying weekday showbread becomes holy. Bread placed on a weekday is neither holy nor does it put the table into use.

phrases.english: This itself is what it teaches us:
that the first use and the making holy of the table
happen on שבת,
as it teaches in the later clause:
And not the candelabrum,
except with its seven lamps in the afternoon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: it states the full rule rather than hinting at a split
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say only that the table's first use needs שבת, while weekday bread still becomes holy
steps.terutzMaskana: Both the first use of the table and the holiness of the bread happen only on שבת, just as the מנורה starts only at its regular evening lighting

steps.title: A one-time case of an individual's incense on the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that incense was once offered for an individual on the outer altar, as a special one-time ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: This is the case where incense was brought for an individual on the outer altar, and it was a one-time ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about a special case of קטרת. It was brought by an individual, and it was burned on the outer altar instead of the inner one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually קטרת is burned on the inner golden altar, and it is a community offering. This ברייתא describes an exception on both counts. It labels that exception a הוראת שעה, meaning it was allowed only for that one time and is not a lasting rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Incense burned in the מקדש
An individual person, as opposed to the community
The outer altar, used for animal offerings
A one-time ruling for a special moment, not a permanent law

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
This is incense that was offered for an individual
phrases.notes: Some versions say זֶהוּ, in round brackets; the corrected wording is זוֹהִי, in square brackets. Both mean 'this is.'

phrases.english: on the outer altar,
and it was a one-time ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: זוֹהִי קְטֹרֶת שֶׁעָלְתָה לְיָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about incense, after the discussion of the שלחן and the מנורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incense was once offered for an individual on the outer altar, as a one-time ruling.

steps.title: Which case is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when this one-time incense of an individual actually happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did this happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which real event the ברייתא is describing. This sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא described an unusual event but did not say when it took place. The גמרא wants to know the specific event.

keyTerms.meaning: Where? In which case?

phrases.english: Where (in which case)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the real case behind the ברייתא in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which event the ברייתא refers to.

steps.title: It was the incense of the נשיאים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that it refers to the incense brought by the נשיאים, the tribal leaders, at the dedication of the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It was with the tribal leaders.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא identifies the case. It was the incense each of the נשיאים brought when the משכן was dedicated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each נשיא brought a spoon full of קטרת as a personal gift. These were individuals, and the incense went on the outer altar. That is why this case was a special one-time ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The leaders of the tribes

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: With the princes.
phrases.notes: The tribal leaders at the dedication of the משכן in במדבר ז, each of whom brought a gift that included incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is the incense of the נשיאים at the dedication of the משכן.

steps.title: Two problems with what the ברייתא implies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out two things the ברייתא seems to suggest. First, an individual may bring incense on the inner altar. Second, the community may bring incense on the outer altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is it only on the outer altar that an individual may not bring incense, so on the inner altar he may? And also, is it only an individual who may not bring it on the outer altar, so the community may?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely and draws out two hidden implications. It is setting up a challenge from another ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא singled out both 'individual' and 'outer altar' as unusual. That could suggest that changing either detail would make it normal. So an individual on the inner altar, or the community on the outer altar, might seem allowed. The גמרא raises both points so it can test them against another source.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner golden altar, where קטרת is normally burned
The community
And furthermore

phrases.english: But is it an individual on the outer altar
that may not,
so on the inner altar he may offer?
And furthermore: on the outer altar
is it only an individual who may not,
so the community may offer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יָחִיד עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן הוּא דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implied meaning of the ברייתא in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implications of the ברייתא in step 25.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming 'individual' and 'outer altar' as unusual suggests that an individual may bring incense inside, and the community may bring it outside. Both of these seem wrong.

steps.title: A ברייתא: an individual may not donate incense even on the inner altar
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא learns from a פסוק that an individual may not donate incense like the נשיאים did, even on the inner altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: You might think an individual could donate incense like this as a gift, and I would apply to it 'Keep what comes out of your lips and do it.' So the פסוק says: 'Do not offer strange incense upon it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that contradicts the first implication. An individual may not bring incense on the inner altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a source, one might think incense is like any other gift: if you promise it, you must bring it. But the פסוק 'Do not offer strange incense upon it' is about the inner golden altar. It forbids donated incense there. This undoes the first implication from step 28.

keyTerms.meaning: Volunteers to give something as a gift
A voluntary gift offering
'Strange' incense, meaning incense that was not commanded
The פסוק teaches

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
One might think an individual may volunteer
and bring something like it as a gift,
phrases.notes: 'Like it' means incense like the incense the נשיאים brought.

phrases.english: and I would apply to it
"What comes out of your lips you shall keep and do"?
The verse says:
"You shall not offer strange incense upon it."
phrases.notes: שמות 30:9. 'Upon it' is the inner golden altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that contradicts the first implication raised in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that an individual may bring incense on the inner altar.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק explicitly forbids donated incense on the inner altar, so an individual may not bring it there either.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: maybe only an individual is excluded
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that perhaps only an individual is forbidden to donate incense, since he never has an obligation to bring incense.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that only an individual may not bring it, because he never brings an obligatory offering like it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and starts a new 'you might think' step about the community. It is setting up the next part of the ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that a person can only donate the kind of offering he is ever required to bring. An individual is never required to bring incense, so he cannot donate it. This suggests the community might be different, since it does bring incense as an obligation. The ברייתא will need to address that, which connects to the second implication from step 28.

keyTerms.meaning: His obligatory offering
Similar to it

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the ברייתא's conclusion. It is a 'you might think' step that will be answered next. Do not take it as the final law that the community may donate incense.

phrases.english: One might think that only an individual may not bring it,
since he does not bring an obligatory offering like it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא as step 29 and moves toward the community.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that the community may bring incense on the outer altar.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא begins to examine whether the community, which does bring obligatory incense, might be allowed to donate it. This sets up a ruling that will address the second implication from step 28.
